lead: `target/release/nvs.exe` is whatever the *last* session built, and rebuilding it costs two minutes for a verdict the debug binary already gives.
body: A `.nvst` case a stale binary fails may simply predate it, and `cargo build --release -p nvs-cli` relinks the world for a one-line edit. Build `cargo build` and run `target/debug/nvs.exe`: it is the binary the driver builds after every acceptance check, so it is the cheap answer and usually the faithful one. `bun nv proofs` builds its own binary first, `target/proof/` for `--bless`, `--run` and `--verify` and `target/release/` for `--record-perf`, so make every `crates/` edit of the group before the first of those calls, because each edit buys another build.
